scientific_hypothesis: Does public EE-response classification trained at one fixed normalized native arm-command amplitude remain valid when the truth-hidden command amplitude changes? Falsify 32/32 original within-distribution success without retraining, optionally test an independently predeclared affine command-aware class-center rule.
source_model: No learned PPO or new training; same prior fixed eight calibration seeds per robot and frozen reference model
controller_native_arm_movement: Original exact normalized native requested_native(t) steps t0/t1 unmodified; multiply only requested_native(2) by declared factor if actually applied, else deliver zero; t3 common native zero probe; t4 action calculated to restore held commanded target POSITION.
decision_if_ambiguous: refuse correction; count abstention and failure
distances: euclidean XYZ from public EE motion to empirical truth response model
linear_command_conditioned_mean: held_calibrated_mean + amplitude*(applied_calibrated_mean_at_1.0 - held_calibrated_mean); hold class mean unchanged; all empirical training class radii unchanged, no look at heldout labels
reject_negative: 0/32 confident mistakes has no statistical zero-risk meaning; all false confident authorizations and abstentions are disclosed even if commanded target error is small
metrics: actual native arm action and physical probe xyz logged
source calibration hash and original seed-split provenance
adversarial_gate: Original 32/32 result was for one fixed command schedule: do NOT claim generic robot/controller OOD or task policy success. If either method confidently wrong, report exact raw case, do not tune training radius/offset on this evaluation.
